correctness.rationale: For arbitrary positive effects (not assumed commuting), the identity \(N=\sum_j(\lambda_jI-T)P_j(\lambda_jI-T)\succeq0\) proves positivity. For adjacent nodes, their pairwise product polynomial is nonnegative on every outcome, hence \(N\succeq(T-\lambda_iI)(\lambda_{i+1}I-T)\) in Loewner order. Continuous spectral hat effects attain the fixed-support scalar spectral bound. In the four-node optimization \(E(a)<(1-a)^2/4\) forces two interior nodes into opposite spectral bands. Their outer midpoint errors bound \(u,v\ge s_a\), while the inner endpoint forces \(\|N\|\ge(s_a-a)(s_a+a)=E(a)\). The symmetric support attains equality; strict monotonicity proves uniqueness. The endpoint \(a=0\) is included, while \(a=1\) is excluded. The full analytical argument is in RESULT.md. The packaged checker passed 3,957 deterministic grouped finite instances, including 450 noncommuting POVMs.

value.rationale: The two-band intrinsic-noise floor is a quantitative counterpart to the impossibility of exact finite-atomic reproduction of \((I,T,T^2)\) on an infinite spectrum. The precise optimal codebook and gap-dependent coefficient govern worst-state extra variance independently of spectral multiplicity. There is strict improvement over choosing the spectral band endpoints, and a polynomial Loewner certificate shows noncommuting measurements cannot improve the optimum. This is a natural complete finite-outcome moment problem, not a reparametrized existing constant or an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
